The paired-surgical arm confirmed intratumoral drug concentrations sufficient for CDK4/6 inhibition, which the palbociclib failure (Taal 2018) had not achieved. Safety data not fully published; full per-term toxicities will become available with the planned manuscript — capture them then.

notes: Negative trial — closed early for futility. The contrast with the abemaciclib recurrent GBM trial (Wen, NCT02981940) is informative: palbociclib has poor CNS penetration (Pgp substrate) and the trial did not require CDKN2A loss; abemaciclib has substantially better CNS penetration and the trial was biomarker-selected. The right lesson is that CDK4/6 inhibitor selection AND biomarker selection both matter — palbociclib failure does not refute the CDK4/6 pathway in CDKN2A-loss GBM.

Anvumetostat is the most clinically-mature MTA-cooperative PRMT5 inhibitor and the safety/efficacy profile here anchors the rationale for BGB-58067 (brain-penetrant successor) and the broader MTA-cooperative class. The four-of-six false-positive CDKN2A-only-call enrollment finding is why central MTAP IHC is mandatory across the class — directly relevant to this patient's diagnostic gate plan.

notes: Sponsor announcement Nov 2024 (Tango Therapeutics 8-K and ESMO presentation): TNG908 discontinued in GBM because CSF samples confirmed inadequate brain exposure, not because of toxicity. Decision-relevant context for this case: it explains why BGB-58067 — the BeiGene brain-penetrant successor with explicit CNS exposure modeling in the IND — became the new lead asset for MTAP-deleted GBM, and why TNG462 (Tango's peripheral-only follow-on) excludes primary CNS tumors. Patient was eligible for TNG908 GBM expansion when it was open; now must wait for BGB-58067 (NCT07485049) or navlimetostat (NCT07492680, MountainTAP-5). Safety reporting limited to the press-release abstract — PubMed/PMC fallback yielded no peer-reviewed paper; the AE data is held in sponsor presentations only. Mark for backfill when peer review publishes.

notes: Foundational paper for EGFRvIII CAR-T in GBM — demonstrated feasibility and antigen-specific tumor pressure, but also the adaptive resistance via EGFRvIII downregulation and tumor-microenvironment immunosuppression. Per-term AE table is not in the main paper text — sourced from main-text descriptions; user-supplied AE table or supplementary file would be needed to backfill specific events. The Penn lab safety profile across the EGFRvIII CAR program is the broader context.

The 1/18 long-term survivor is the same finding pattern as the O'Rourke STM 2017 paper — durable responses are possible but rare with first-generation single-antigen constructs.

intervention_dose: Nivolumab 3 mg/kg IV q2w vs bevacizumab 10 mg/kg IV q2w, until progression or unacceptable toxicity
population_detail: 369 adults with first-recurrence GBM, KPS >=70, post-Stupp.
median_dor_or_pfs: mOS 9.8 vs 10.0 mo (no difference)

outcomes.name: ORR
outcomes.notes: bevacizumab (much higher response rate but no OS gain)

safety_summary: Nivolumab class safety; bevacizumab class safety (hypertension, proteinuria, bleeding). No new signals.
notes: First randomized phase 3 of an ICI in primary brain tumors. Negative — nivolumab no better than bevacizumab in recurrent GBM. The 7.8% nivolumab ORR is the activity ceiling for ICI monotherapy in unselected recurrent GBM.

intervention_dose: Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV: neoadjuvant dose ~14 days pre-surgery, then resumed q3w post-resection until progression
population_detail: 35 adults with recurrent GBM amenable to repeat resection, KPS >=70. Randomized 16 to neoadjuvant + adjuvant pembrolizumab and 19 to adjuvant-only.
median_dor_or_pfs: mOS 13.7 mo (neoadjuvant arm) vs 7.5 mo (adjuvant-only)

outcomes.name: biomarker
outcomes.notes: neoadjuvant pembrolizumab upregulated T-cell and IFN-gamma gene signatures in resected tumor; downregulated cell-cycle signatures

safety_summary: Manageable. No grade >=3 immune-related AEs attributed to pembrolizumab in either arm. The neoadjuvant timing did not increase perioperative complications.

toxicities.notes: not increased by neoadjuvant pembrolizumab timing

notes: Small randomized trial (n=35) — hypothesis-generating signal that neoadjuvant ICI timing matters more than adjuvant-only in GBM. The OS gain (mOS 13.7 vs 7.5 mo) and the intratumoral immune correlates are the most-cited PD-1 GBM signal. Not enrollable here (recurrent disease), but the principle is influencing trial design across the GBM ICI space.

intervention_label: DCVax-L autologous dendritic-cell vaccine (Liau phase 3 ECC)
intervention_dose: Intradermal DCVax-L vaccinations on days 0, 10, 20 then months 2, 4, 8, 12, then biannual — alongside standard care
population_detail: 331 patients enrolled in the original phase 3 (232 DCVax-L + standard care; 99 randomized to standard care, with crossover allowed). External-control comparison used contemporaneous matched patients from 1,366 control-arm patients in other GBM trials.
design: Phase 3 prospective externally-controlled cohort trial (originally randomized with crossover)
comparator: Matched external control from other GBM trial control arms
median_dor_or_pfs: Newly diagnosed mOS 19.3 vs 16.5 mo (HR 0.80); recurrent mOS 13.2 vs 7.8 mo (HR 0.58)
safety_summary: Well tolerated. Most common AEs were injection-site reactions and low-grade flu-like symptoms. No grade 4-5 events attributed to vaccine.

toxicities.notes: low rate per the primary paper; full per-term table in JAMA Oncology supplement

notes: Methodology is heavily debated. The pivotal phase 3 was originally randomized with crossover; the published 2023 analysis substituted external matched controls instead of the originally-randomized comparator after protocol modifications. ROBINS-I serious risk-of-bias reflects this. The published OS signals (HR 0.80 newly diagnosed; HR 0.58 recurrent) are real but the magnitude is contested because the control choice was retrospective. Decision-relevant for this case because the user explicitly asked for compassionate-use options and DCVax-L has an expanded-access protocol (NCT02146066).

intervention_label: SurVaxM survivin peptide vaccine + adjuvant TMZ
intervention_dose: SurVaxM (SVN53-67/M57-KLH) 500 mcg subcutaneous + sargramostim (GM-CSF) adjuvant, four priming doses every 2 weeks then maintenance monthly, alongside standard adjuvant TMZ
population_detail: 63 adults with newly diagnosed GBM who completed Stupp RT+TMZ without progression; KPS >=70; survivin expression confirmed by IHC.
median_dor_or_pfs: mPFS 11.4 mo; mOS 25.9 mo; 2-yr OS 51%; 3-yr OS 41%

outcomes.name: PFS_rate
outcomes.notes: PFS6 (from start of vaccine, equivalent to 12 months from diagnosis)

safety_summary: Well tolerated. Most common AEs were injection-site reactions and low-grade systemic symptoms (fatigue, flu-like). No serious AEs attributable to SurVaxM.
notes: Phase 2a single-arm — the OS signal (mOS 25.9 mo) is encouraging vs the ~16-month historical control but single-arm with non-contemporaneous comparison. The pivotal randomized phase 2b (SURVIVE, NCT05163080) is the trial that will determine whether this becomes real evidence. Eligible to enroll currently if SURVIVE has open slots; the SurVaxM expanded-access conversation is also available via MimiVax.

intervention_dose: Rindopepimut 500 mcg + GM-CSF intradermal; q2w priming then monthly maintenance, alongside standard adjuvant TMZ
indication: Newly diagnosed EGFRvIII-expressing glioblastoma, minimal residual disease post-RT+TMZ
population_detail: 745 adults with EGFRvIII-positive newly diagnosed GBM, post-resection (>=GTR or minimal residual disease) and completed RT + TMZ without progression. 165 sites in 22 countries.
median_dor_or_pfs: mOS 20.0 vs 20.1 mo (no benefit)

outcomes.name: HR_OS
outcomes.notes: futility met at interim — trial halted

safety_summary: Injection-site reactions were the dominant AE — common but mild grade 1-2. No new safety signals.
notes: Negative phase 3 — rindopepimut did not improve OS in EGFRvIII+ newly diagnosed GBM. Critical caveat for any EGFRvIII-targeted vaccine strategy. The leading hypothesis for failure is antigen escape (EGFRvIII heterogeneous within tumor, lost on relapse) — the same mechanism that limited the first-generation Penn EGFRvIII CAR-T. The lesson influenced subsequent dual-target (EGFR + IL13Ra2) and synNotch designs in this case's E-SYNC and CART-EGFR-IL13Ra2 evidence rows.

intervention_dose: Single intratumoral CAN-3110 injection at escalating doses (1e6 to 1e10 PFU); stereotactic delivery via biopsy needle into enhancing tumor
population_detail: 41 evaluable patients with recurrent HGG, KPS >=70, accessible enhancing tumor for stereotactic injection. Pre-existing HSV-1 serology was the key effect-modifier.
median_dor_or_pfs: mOS 11.6 mo overall; 14.2 mo in HSV-seropositive; 7.8 mo in seronegative

outcomes.name: biomarker
outcomes.notes: T-cell repertoire diversification and IFN-gamma signatures correlated with survival; viral clearance by neutralizing antibody titer was associated with longer survival in seropositive patients

safety_summary: Well tolerated — no dose-limiting toxicities. Most common AEs were transient perilesional edema, headache, and seizure (managed with steroids and antiepileptics).

toxicities.notes: no DLTs across the full dose range
rare; flagged because of this patient's history

notes: FDA Fast Track in 2024 for recurrent HGG. The 14.2-mo mOS in HSV-1-seropositive patients is the strongest signal — translates to ~2x the historical recurrent GBM benchmark. Single-dose, no maintenance. Recurrent-disease only; preposition for second-line conversation. The intratumoral hemorrhage history is a relative caution but not absolute — perilesional inflammation from viral lysis combined with prior bleed warrants explicit screening team conversation.

intervention_dose: Single intratumoral PVSRIPO infusion via convection-enhanced delivery (CED) catheter; dose 5.0e7 TCID50 (RP2D after escalation)
population_detail: 61 adults with recurrent supratentorial GBM, KPS >=70, single contrast-enhancing lesion 1-5 cm amenable to CED catheter placement. Single-center Duke.
median_dor_or_pfs: mOS 12.5 mo; 24- and 36-mo OS plateau at 21%
safety_summary: Most common AEs were transient peritumoral inflammation, edema, hemiparesis, and seizure — typically grade 1-2 and managed with steroids. No PVSRIPO-related neuropoliomyelitis.

toxicities.notes: the index safety concern; no events

notes: The 21% OS plateau at 24 and 36 months is the standout finding — substantially above historical recurrent GBM controls (~14%). Phase 2 readout (Desjardins 2025, PMID 40313264) confirmed mOS ~7-12 mo across cohorts and the long-tail plateau. Recurrent disease only; CED delivery requires accessible single lesion. Pre-position for second-line conversation.

intervention_dose: Single intratumoral PVSRIPO infusion via CED; 5.0e7 TCID50
indication: Recurrent WHO grade IV malignant glioma
population_detail: 121 patients pooled across two phase 2 cohorts at Duke and partner sites. KPS >=70, single CED-accessible lesion.
median_dor_or_pfs: mOS 7.0 mo (monotherapy arm); 24-mo OS plateau ~19%

outcomes.name: OS
outcomes.notes: monotherapy arm; updated from the 2018 phase 1 signal

safety_summary: Consistent with the 2018 phase 1 — peritumoral inflammation and edema were the dominant signals, managed with steroids.

toxicities.notes: specific rate in the CCR supplement

notes: Phase 2 update — mOS lower than the 2018 phase 1 (7.0 vs 12.5 mo) but the 24-mo OS plateau (~19%) confirms the long-tail benefit pattern. Randomized phase 2 vs lomustine (NCT06177964) is the next maturation.

exclusion_reason: Toca 511 program discontinued after the negative TOCA 5 phase 3 readout (Sept 2019, n=403). Drug is not enrollable; including for context only in a note on the oncolytic axis. The early-phase signal (Cloughesy 2018 Cancer Discovery) of durable CR did not survive the phase 3 confirmatory trial.
notes: Sponsor Tocagen discontinued the program. Logged as audit-trail context for why the oncolytic-virus axis is concentrated on CAN-3110 and PVSRIPO and not on the broader Toca platform.

intervention_label: SonoCloud-9 microbubble-enhanced focused ultrasound BBB opening + nab-paclitaxel
intervention_dose: SonoCloud-9 implanted FUS device; q3w cycles of FUS (target peri-tumoral BBB opening) + nab-paclitaxel 40-260 mg/m2 IV (dose-escalation)
indication: Recurrent glioblastoma — peri-tumoral BBB disruption to enable systemic chemotherapy delivery
population_detail: 17 adults with recurrent GBM, KPS >=60, surgically implanted with the SonoCloud-9 skull device at time of resection. Single-center Northwestern.
effect_size: 4-6x increased peri-tumoral drug concentration vs unsonicated tissue; up to 6 cycles tolerated
median_dor_or_pfs: Not the primary endpoint; efficacy signal not the focus of this phase 1

outcomes.name: biomarker
outcomes.notes: 4-6x increased peri-tumoral nab-paclitaxel concentration vs unsonicated brain

outcomes.name: DCR
outcomes.notes: preliminary disease-control signals; full survival analysis pending follow-on trial

safety_summary: Generally well tolerated. Implantation procedure was performed at the time of tumor resection; no implant-related deaths. Transient FUS-related transient edema was the main on-treatment signal.

toxicities.notes: no implant-related deaths or device explants required

notes: First-in-human skull-implantable FUS device for repeated peri-tumoral BBB opening in GBM. The 4-6x drug-delivery enhancement is the proof-of-mechanism signal; the survival data is not yet mature. Decision-relevant for this case as the delivery-enhancement principle that could rescue any antibody-class or large-molecule CNS therapy (including pembrolizumab + FUS in the Leddon NCT07385846 dMMR trial).

intervention_dose: Bevacizumab 10 mg/kg IV q2w (monotherapy arm); or bevacizumab 10 mg/kg q2w + irinotecan 340 or 125 mg/m2 q2w
population_detail: 167 adults with recurrent GBM (first or second relapse), KPS >=70. Randomized 1:1 to bevacizumab monotherapy or bevacizumab + irinotecan.
median_dor_or_pfs: mPFS 4.2 mo (bev mono); ORR 28%
safety_summary: Hypertension, fatigue, headache, and proteinuria were the most common AEs. Grade >=3 intracranial hemorrhage 2.4% — the central safety concern.

toxicities.notes: the central concern for this case given the patient's intratumoral hemorrhage history
characteristic of anti-VEGF therapy near surgical sites

notes: BRAIN study supported FDA accelerated approval of bevacizumab for recurrent GBM. CRITICAL safety flag in this case: the patient presented with intratumoral hemorrhage, which is the most cited relative contraindication for bevacizumab. Carry forward as a recurrence option only after explicit re-imaging and bleeding-risk reassessment with the treating team.

intervention_dose: Lomustine 90 mg/m2 PO q6w + bevacizumab 10 mg/kg IV q2w, until progression or unacceptable toxicity
population_detail: 437 adults with recurrent GBM, WHO PS 0-2, post-Stupp.
median_dor_or_pfs: mOS 9.1 vs 8.6 mo (no OS benefit); mPFS 4.2 vs 1.5 mo (PFS gain)

outcomes.name: HR_OS
outcomes.notes: no OS benefit — primary endpoint failed

safety_summary: Bevacizumab class AEs (hypertension, proteinuria, bleeding) + lomustine cytopenias. Grade >=3 AE rate 64% (combo) vs 38% (lomustine alone). Treatment-related deaths: 4 vs 4 (similar).

toxicities.notes: low absolute rate but the critical concern for this case

notes: PFS gain but no OS benefit — the published statement of recurrent-GBM bevacizumab activity. Together with BRAIN it defines the recurrence bevacizumab option set. Same intratumoral-hemorrhage caveat applies as on the Friedman 2009 row.
